title: Adaptive quant routing and kernel dispatcher for heterogeneous precision paths
creator: Aisha Menon
description: Implement an adaptive routing layer in the serving runtime that selects and dispatches execution kernels across FP16/FP8/INT8 code paths based on per-request quantization profile, model calibration metadata, and live performance signals. This ticket covers the dispatcher strategy, per-model profile format, calibration integration, offline accuracy validation hooks, and a plan for safe rollout with fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can read a model quantization profile (JSON) at load-time and expose it to the dispatcher
Dispatcher makes kernel selection decisions deterministically given (model, sequence_length, batch_size, profile) and logs decision metadata to tracing
Calibration step outputs per-layer scaling/zero-point metadata that the runtime can consume for INT8/FP8 fast paths
End-to-end accuracy validation harness runs for a model and produces a pass/fail based on configurable degradation thresholds
Automated fallback to FP16 for kernels that fail numeric checks during warmup or when metrics exceed thresholds

Benchmark: mixed-precision dispatch path achieves target median token latency improvement of >=12% vs baseline FP16 for median sequence length workload with <0.8% task quality degradation as measured by acceptance suite
tasks: Define quantization profile schema (per-op/per-layer, supported dtypes, calibration versioning)
Implement profile loader and validation at model load in runtime
Build kernel dispatcher component with rule engine (profile overrides, heuristics lookup, dynamic signal inputs)
Integrate calibration artifacts (scale/zero) into kernel API and memory layout
Add tracing/logging for chosen path + reason code for each dispatched op
Create offline calibration workflow script that emits profiles from a calibration dataset
Implement accuracy validation harness (prompt set runner, metrics, threshold config)
Write unit and integration tests, including synthetic numeric-stress tests and end-to-end generation checks
Prepare canary rollout and rollback plan + runtime feature flag
design_notes: Profile schema: JSON with fields: version, model_hash, op_entries[{op_name, op_type, preferred_dtype, fallback_dtype, layer_scope, calibration_version}]
Heuristic ordering: prefer lower-precision path if (calibrated && estimated_quant_error < layer_threshold && expected_latency_gain > min_gain)
Dispatcher will consult: static profile, runtime perf model (small table lookup by batch/seq), and live telemetry (GPU memory pressure, recent kernel error counts)
Numeric safety: warmup run of first N requests in permissive validation mode where numeric deltas are logged and compared against reference FP16 outputs
Fallback semantics: per-op fallback to higher precision for a single request if numeric check fails; escalate to model-level rollback if error rate > 0.5% over sliding window
calibration_workflow_steps: 1) Collect representative calibration corpus for the model (min 10k tokens across usage patterns)
2) Run offline calibrator that collects activation statistics (min/max, histogram, moments) per layer
3) Compute per-channel/per-tensor scale and zero-point (INT8) and exponent bias for FP8 profiles
4) Produce signed profile artifact with checksums and calibration metadata (dataset id, date, calibrator version)
5) Upload profile to model registry and tag model version with calibration_id
6) Optionally run reduced accuracy validation (subset prompts) before wide deployment
accuracy_validation_plan: Validation harness will run a curated acceptance prompt set (approx 2k prompts covering Q/A, summarization, instruction following)
Metrics captured: token-level KL divergence vs FP16 reference, top-1 token agreement, task-specific metrics (QA F1, Rouge-L for summarization), and embedding cosine drift
Pass criteria defaults: top-1 token agreement >= 99.2% AND task metric drop <= 0.8% for P0 models. Thresholds configurable per-customer.
Validation will be repeatable and seed-controlled; results stored in benchmarking dashboard with model_hash and calibration_id
If a model fails, detector produces per-prompt diff logs to help calibrator adjustments (per-layer thresholds and re-run suggestions)
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Dev): enable dispatcher behind feature flag; smoke tests against small GPU pool
Stage 2 (Canary): 5% traffic on dedicated queue with verbose numeric logging; monitor error rates and divergence metrics
Stage 3 (Ramp): 25% traffic with automated rollback if divergence thresholds crossed or latency regressions observed
Stage 4 (GA): full traffic when 72h canary stability and benchmark pass achieved
Emergency rollback: runtime flag to globally force FP16 path; retain last-known-good calibration_id for each model
dependencies: ENG-10077 - model registry: add calibration_id field
ENG-10234 - tracing: extend per-op reason_code and metrics API
ENG-10350 - kernel library: expose fast path that accepts calibration metadata buffers
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: calibration mismatch between offline dataset and production leading to quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative default fallbacks, per-model thresholds, and short canaries
Risk: performance regressions for short sequences where fusion benefits are lost. Mitigation: incorporate sequence-length-aware heuristics and prefer FP16 for seq<16 by default
Risk: increased complexity in debugging production incidents. Mitigation: enriched tracing with reason codes and chunked numeric diffs uploaded to secure S3 for on-call diagnosis
test_plan: Unit tests for profile parser and validator (including malformed/old-version profiles)
Integration tests running small model with both FP16/FP8/INT8 kernels and numeric assertions
End-to-end nightly benchmark that runs acceptance prompts vs FP16 baseline and records metrics
Chaos test: simulated kernel failures to verify per-op fallback and model rollback logic
